points.title: Biometrics
points.must: Authentication by unique physical or behavioural characteristics compared with a stored template; examples: fingerprint, face, iris, voice.

points.title: Physical and behavioural biometrics
points.must: Physical = what the body is like (fingerprint, iris, face); behavioural = how you do something (voice, signature, typing rhythm).

points.title: How biometric log-in works
points.must: Enrolment creates a template; a new scan is compared with it; a similarity score above the threshold is accepted.

points.title: False rejection and false acceptance
points.must: False rejection: the right user is refused; false acceptance: a stranger is let in (more dangerous); a stricter threshold gives fewer false acceptances but more false rejections.

points.title: Advantages and disadvantages of biometrics
points.must: Unique, cannot be forgotten, lost or shared; but expensive, false rejections / acceptances, privacy — cannot be changed if stolen.

points.title: Two-factor authentication
points.must: Two different types of evidence — something you know, have, are; a stolen password alone is not enough; two passwords are not two factors.

points.title: Authentication and authorisation
points.must: Authentication = who you are; authorisation = what you are allowed to do (access rights).

points.title: Strong passwords and a password policy
points.must: Long, mixed characters, not dictionary words, different for each account; policy: lockout after wrong attempts, stored as (salted) hashes, 2FA.

points.title: Attacks on passwords
points.must: At least two of: brute force, dictionary attack, credential stuffing, phishing, shoulder surfing, keylogger.

points.title: Access rights, least privilege, audit trail
points.must: Rights such as read only / read and write set per user or group; each user gets only the access needed for the job; an audit trail records who did what and when.

points.title: Types of malware
points.must: Virus, worm, Trojan, spyware, ransomware — what each does.

points.title: How anti-virus software works
points.must: Signature-based detection (needs updates, misses new malware) vs heuristic / behaviour detection (finds new malware); real-time scanning; quarantine.

points.title: Other countermeasures and an infected computer
points.must: Updates, no unknown attachments, scan USB drives, trusted downloads, backups, training; if infected: disconnect, scan, change passwords, restore from backup.

points.title: Phishing
points.must: Fake e-mails or messages that trick people into revealing passwords or bank details; signs (urgency, generic greeting, fake sender or link) and what to do.

points.title: Other social engineering
points.must: At least two of: spear phishing, smishing / vishing, pharming, pretexting, shoulder surfing, baiting.
